column1: # BATCH 06 — pitch layout most=G high=E mid=G low=E least=G
# Elevated slots are high (LANE A — cannot be undone) and low (LANE B — gets to see
# inside). Lane declared per row below; the test is answered before any prose exists.
# === umami-roasted-black — insightful / omniscient / unseeing
# AXIS: one observation about a person and something they had never understood
#   rearranges itself. Roasted — you say it out loud, unprompted, in the room.
# NOT: perceptive (sour-fermented-black — noticing), observant (umami-fermented-edamame
#   — detail). Insightful is the read that EXPLAINS somebody to themselves.
# PERCEPTION TRAIT — the two obvious moves both fail. Stating the perception ("you can
#   see she is frightened of him") makes Accept agreement with a portrait; stripping it
#   leaves the act arbitrary. Each facet: one concrete deniable signal, the rest of the
#   scene pointing the other way, and an act out of proportion to the signal. Never
#   write the inference.
# OFF-LIMITS: snowy owl and the lemming under the snow; "seeing through everybody is
#   lonely work"; "the load-bearing detail turns up on a walk"; "fine can just mean
#   fine"; "people change without telling anybody"; bacon fat, garlic. QUESTION owns: the
#   friend on the phone about a row with her sister. OLD FACETS: ten minutes with a
#   couple and the whole marriage, the remark about her father, who is really running the
#   meeting, the divided room taken at face value, last to know those two are together.

# LANE A high: said in the week her dad is dying, and she cannot unhear it.
# LANE B low: gets to see how a saleroom actually works — who is not bidding, and why.
# === umami-fried-adzuki — passionate / combustible / dispassionate
# AXIS: what you care about you care about at full volume and immediately, and it pulls
#   other people in. There is no mild setting on the dial.
# NOT: zealous (spicy-boiled-green — cause), ardent (sweet-fried-black — devotion),
#   driven (spicy-fried-cannellini — ambition). This is the heat of caring, expressed at
#   once, because fried means no gap between feeling and saying.
# OFF-LIMITS: andalusian fighting a paper bag; "feeling it that strongly puts everyone
#   else on eggshells"; "feeling shows in the voice before the words"; "wait until you
#   have cooled off"; "caring less about it costs you nothing"; soy salt, hot oil.
#   QUESTION owns: the meeting about closing the library. OLD FACETS: the committee and
#   the playing field, the jury past lunch, the phone-in's forty seconds, the taken-back
#   move, the union rep on the factory floor. ALSO: four of those five are meetings,
#   votes or committees — that whole register is spent.

# LANE A high: five o'clock, and after five o'clock it cannot be undone.
# LANE B low: gets to see a director take his own film apart in front of the people who
#   love it.
# === sour-boiled-navy — literal-minded / wooden / elliptical
# AXIS: you answer the question that was asked, exactly, and hinting at a thing rather
#   than saying it strikes you as a wasted sentence. Boiled — patiently, at length.
# NOT: precise (sour-boiled-cannellini, batch 02 — accuracy of the figure; keep this one
#   about LANGUAGE, and do not go near scales or measurements), plain (sour-dried-butter
#   — register). Literal-minded is subtext not being a channel you receive on.
# OFF-LIMITS: parrot repeating it exactly; "take it all literally and the meaning walks
#   off unnoticed"; "plain words prevent most arguments"; "read between the lines here";
#   "half of what's meant is never said"; cider vinegar, mustard. QUESTION owns: the
#   house sale, the survey, the wobbling buyer. OLD FACETS: the contract clause and the
#   definition of month, how long the drive was, two hundred grams and the scales, the
#   thing about her sister, answering in the same key about somebody else.
sour-boiled-navy

# LANE A high: it goes on the certificate and is cut once.
# LANE B low: gets to see a betting shop working — the board, and the way the regulars
#   say things sideways.
# === spicy-smoked-edamame — feisty / scrappy / docile
# AXIS: half the size of the argument and still in it at the end, having won the part
#   that mattered. You go in first and small, before the thing grows.
# NOT: firm (sour-dried-navy, batch 05 — not yielding to who is asking), challenging
#   (sour-fried-kidney), combative. Feisty is disproportionate fight from a small
#   position, and smoked keeps it small — no speeches.
# OFF-LIMITS: wolverine taking a kill off a bear; "go in first and small, before it grows
#   a committee"; "size settles fewer arguments than people expect"; "pay the small
#   unfair thing and keep the day"; "some fights cost more than they return"; chipotle
#   salt, mesquite. QUESTION owns: the builder with an answer for everything. OLD FACETS:
#   the parking space stand-off, the planning refusal, the market stall price, the charge
#   on the letter, the girl on the phone with the policy. NOTE: two of those five are
#   arguments about a price — that shape is spent.
spicy-smoked-edamame

# LANE A high: once two hundred people disperse there is no bus, and no second chance
#   to ask for one.
# LANE B low: gets to see how a festival site runs — numbered pitches, stewards on
#   radios, and the rule that nobody gets moved after midnight.
# === sweet-dried-chickpea — wholesome / sanitised / unsavoury
# AXIS: old-fashioned things done sincerely — the walk, the phone call, the birthday
#   remembered — and the edges quietly filed off the story.
# NOT: kind (sweet-boiled-cannellini — warmth toward a person), earnest
#   (sour-roasted-black — sincerity of belief). Wholesome is the clean version, meant.
# OFF-LIMITS: shetland pony safe with anybody's children; "keep it clean and they'll ask
#   you to speak"; "the kind version and the true version are usually both available";
#   "nobody needs the joke cleaned up"; "go for the long walk and tell nobody where";
#   cardamom sugar. QUESTION owns: the nephew's school project on a grandad who drank,
#   told jokes and left for two years — so no cleaned-up account of a dead relative given
#   to a child. OLD FACETS: the version of your father for the grandchildren (which also
#   makes the reader a grandparent), the village show tent (banned village scenery), the
#   two true kind stories, the joke that is nearly too much, the stag weekend.

# LANE A high: it is cut into stone once and stands there for everybody afterwards.
# LANE B low: gets to see a snooker hall at closing — the lights over each table, the
#   man who racks up, what the room is like when the tables go dark one at a time.
# ============ COLD READ (final text, three lists) ============
# umami-roasted-black
#  most  PAGE: the boyfriend says they have decided not to do presents; she agrees half a
#        second after; the barbecue thinks they are wonderful; four years together.
#        ACT: them both, the table, that decision. POLE: excess needs (a) evidence the
#        read is right — the half second — and (b) evidence it is uninvited, which is
#        that nobody asked and everybody else finds them lovely. Resist = you keep it.
#        Perception rule: signal deniable, scene pointing the other way, inference never
#        stated on the page.
#  high  PAGE: your friend's dad has days; her brother has not been once; a week of her
#        telling everybody what that makes him; the ward sister's remark about somebody
#        ringing after eleven with no name. ACT: her, and who that is. POLE: the read is
#        the join between the caller and the brother; Resist = you let her go on thinking
#        it. BREAK FIXED: opened on "Her dad" with no antecedent anywhere for "her".
#        LANE A: days left, so it cannot be unheard before he dies.
#  mid   PAGE: eleven of you; the last night; going well; one went to the bar the moment
#        the other came in and has not been back; the table gets sorted for food.
#        ACT: the chair, the two of them. POLE: mild — small signal, small act. Resist =
#        you sit anywhere.
#  low   PAGE: the same four dealers every week; none bidding against another all morning;
#        twice the auctioneer calling bids nobody made; you get the chest for about what
#        you expected. ACT: your friend, a good day. POLE: unseeing needs the evidence
#        present and unread, and all three signals are on the page. Resist = you notice.
#        LANE B: how a saleroom actually works, and who is not bidding.
#  least PAGE: your sister rings; the tests since March; everybody has known for weeks;
#        you have spoken to your mum every Sunday in that time. ACT: your sister, the
#        not-telling. POLE: the weekly calls are the evidence. Resist = you would have
#        known.
# umami-fried-adzuki
#  most  PAGE: the housewarming; the estate called rough; twenty minutes into him; the
#        second half of what he said; he was agreeing. ACT: the point. POLE: combustible
#        needs the heat landing on an ally and the reader continuing anyway — both on the
#        page. Resist = you stop.
#  high  PAGE: eleven weeks; the decision made this morning; it happens at five; it is
#        three; you only came in to walk him. ACT: the rescues, the phone. POLE: the
#        caring is out of proportion to your relation to the dog, which is the trait.
#        Resist = you walk him and go. LANE A: five o'clock, and after it nothing.
#  mid   PAGE: the band made the record themselves; eleven copies; the man's line about
#        the third one this month. ACT: him, what is on it, four of the eleven. POLE:
#        argument plus money. Resist = you let it go.
#  low   PAGE: the film that got you through nineteen; the director present; forty minutes
#        of him taking it apart; six of you came out for it. ACT: the drink, something
#        else. POLE: dispassionate needs the thing that SHOULD provoke feeling, and it is
#        named. Resist = you would be upset. LANE B: a director dismantling his own film
#        in front of the people who love it.
#  least PAGE: two friends arguing the whole way; whether to cancel; your money in it;
#        they stop and ask you. ACT: them. POLE: your own money is the evidence that not
#        minding is real rather than polite. Resist = you have a view.
# sour-boiled-navy
#  most  PAGE: the bags in your dad's boot; your mother asking whether you are eating
#        properly; what she wants is a call; he drove forty minutes to say it.
#        ACT: him, this week's food. POLE: wooden needs the real request visible to the
#        reader and missed by you — both there — and the forty minutes is the cost.
#        Resist = you ring her. FIXED: "the boot" presumed the reader owns a car; it is
#        his, and he has just driven it here.
#  high  PAGE: the registrar reading back what goes on the certificate; your aunt wanting
#        "at home"; kinder and nearly true. ACT: the registrar, where he actually died —
#        which the line supplies by contrast. POLE: the true wording against the kind one.
#        Resist = you let the kind version stand. LANE A: it is on the certificate.
#  mid   PAGE: the man in the bike shop; ten seconds; "fine for another winter"; two
#        things it could mean; riding home in the dark. ACT: him, the word fine. POLE:
#        mild — one vague word queried. Resist = you take "fine". FIXED: "looked at it"
#        never named the bike.
#  low   PAGE: the board in a hand nobody explains; the man in since opening writing
#        nothing down; the favourite in the two o'clock has had a very long trip up.
#        ACT: your five pounds, something else. POLE: elliptical mild — you act on an
#        implication nobody stated. Resist = you hear a remark about travel. FIXED: the
#        draft went two inferences deep ("got at", then which horse he meant), and the
#        clarity pass requires a single read. LANE B: a betting shop working, and the way
#        the regulars say things sideways.
#  least PAGE: your partner asks straight out; her work thing at the weekend; you do not
#        want to go; saying so would land badly; she has asked twice. ACT: her, the week.
#        POLE: you make her infer rather than answering. Resist = you say no.
# spicy-smoked-edamame
#  most  PAGE: the sign; four pence a litre; about two pounds; the man already out to look
#        at it; three cars waiting behind you. ACT: his manager. POLE: scrappy is the
#        disproportion — two pounds against three cars and a second escalation. Resist =
#        you pay and go.
#  high  PAGE: the last train cancelled; two hundred people told to come back; once they
#        scatter there is nobody to lay anything on for; the man with the radio walking
#        away. ACT: him, a bus. POLE: first and small, before it grows. Resist = you go
#        home. LANE A: the crowd disperses and the chance goes with it.
#  mid   PAGE: two people called through before you; the woman not looking up; fifty
#        minutes; the appointment time on your phone. ACT: the desk, saying so. POLE:
#        small, early, once — the smoked version of the trait. Resist = you wait.
#  low   PAGE: numbered pitches; the steward with the radio says he CAN move the tent; the
#        two in it asleep since ten. ACT: the far pitch, the bins. POLE FAILURE FOUND AND
#        FIXED, and this is what the third list is for: the draft had a rule that the
#        steward could move nobody after midnight, so taking the worse pitch was the only
#        thing available rather than a disposition — Resist had no foothold whatever. The
#        referents were all fine and it would have passed the old two lists. LANE B still
#        stands: numbered pitches and stewards on radios.
#  least PAGE: the thing was yours; head office being told otherwise; you standing there;
#        the one being thanked knows. ACT: the work. POLE: docile fully — you ask for
#        nothing while the evidence sits on the page. Resist = you say it was yours.
# sweet-dried-chickpea
#  most  PAGE: the new girlfriend's question; the six of you at university; the whole
#        afternoon; the year one of you was very ill; another one left because of it.
#        ACT: her, the funny version. POLE: sanitised needs the removed material NAMED,
#        or there is no removal to vote on. Resist = you tell her.
#  high  PAGE: your grandad's stone to the mason this week; cut once; your aunt's verse
#        that would suit anybody; he answered the phone the same way for forty years.
#        ACT: that phrase, which is on the page. POLE: sincerity against the generic.
#        Resist = you take the verse. BREAK FIXED: opened with "He" and nothing had
#        established that anybody had died. LANE A: cut once, and it stands afterwards.
#  mid   PAGE: the card must go today; your aunt's birthday; the queue out to the door;
#        no reply in four years. ACT: the queue, the stamp, the card. POLE: sincere and
#        unreciprocated, which is the whole of it. Resist = you do not bother. BREAK
#        FIXED: "her birthday" had no antecedent.
#  low   PAGE: the man turning the light off over each table; the room going dark in
#        sections; yours the last lit; the joke that is nearly too much; the other three
#        still deciding. ACT: the laugh. POLE: you go with it before judging it, and the
#        three deciding are what make that a choice. Resist = you do not laugh. LANE B: a
#        snooker hall at closing.
#  least PAGE: four in the morning; the taxi; her question; it does not make you look
#        good; two of the people in it are her friends. ACT: her, the night, the worst
#        part. POLE: unsavoury fully — told willingly, to the wrong audience. Resist =
#        you edit it.
